reason: The dense knot and cold cloud seem like the most direct way to investigate whether the surviving clumps can form stars.
expectation: The cold gas may feed the knot and lead to new stars, though it may first create an intermediate gathering.

alternatives.reason: The young stars interacting with dust could address the other goal, but I want to follow the surviving clumps first.

effect: The surviving clumps formed stars, completing that goal; I can now follow the dust.
reaction: Satisfying to see material from the old pillars become new stars.
reason: I'll follow the dust that remains near the young stars before exploring its outward journey.
expectation: The stars' light may illuminate or heat the nearby dust, though I'm unsure what form the result will take.

alternatives.reason: The outflow could carry dust away, but I want to see the effect of the stars' light first.

effect: The dust absorbs starlight and radiates in infrared; the remaining goal may also require following dust outward.
reaction: The distinction between glowing gas and warmed dust is interesting.
reason: Combining the warmed dust with the outflow follows its possible journey away from the nursery.
expectation: The outflow may carry the warmed dust outward, though I'm unsure whether it survives unchanged.

alternatives.reason: This could also trace dust in the outflow, but I want to follow the warmed dust first.

effect: The warmed dust joined the outflow, with some grains sheltered and others exposed; I can now follow it into the outer gas.
reaction: I'm curious whether the grains survive the hot surroundings.
reason: This is the only offered combination and continues the dust's journey.
expectation: The hot outer gas may disperse or erode the dust, though some grains might survive.

effect: The hot outer gas eroded much of the carried dust, completing the inherited-dust goal and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast between earlier warming and later grain destruction was a satisfying conclusion to that journey.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the surviving clumps into new stars was most worthwhile: it gave material from the old pillars a clear later role.

leastWorthwhile.text: Carrying the warmed dust into the outflow was a fairly predictable transition, though it set up the final result.

surprise.text: The distinction between gas glowing through atomic processes and dust radiating absorbed heat sharpened my understanding of the different kinds of light.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless; the final combination was the only offered action, but it clearly continued the dust's journey.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: following familiar material through different environments made me curious about its further fate.
